_readme: STAGE 3 OF ONE WATER ON THE TREE: AN IMPACT IN THE WINDOW (2026-10-27, docs/WATER_V2.md 14.4). A 30 m stone at
20 km/s into the sea 7 km east of the Merrimack's mouth, ten minutes into the solver's spin-up hour, on the bar
scene's pinned clocks: its cavity (1.3 km across, to the bed) is IMPOSED on the solver's columns at its instant,
at mip 0 and on the twin, and the law carries it -- no analytic reader inside the window; the edge's exterior
reads the Bessel law as every edge does. The gate: the first crest's arrival at the anchor and the sea points
against the Bessel law's and against sqrt(g h0), within 10 % ('[swe] the probe' every batch for the hour after,
the law's level in brackets; '[impact] stage 3' says where it fell and what lies under it).
